pages.caption: Once upon a time there lived in a certain village a little country girl
pages.scene: A certain village nestled in the countryside. Modest cottages line a quiet dirt road. The sun shines on a peaceful rural community.

pages.caption: The beauty of whom was everywhere the principal theme of conversation
pages.scene: The same village. Townspeople gather in small groups, whispering and gesturing about someone.

pages.caption: But particularly at her mother's, who was passionately fond of her
pages.scene: Inside a modest country home. A mother holds her daughter close, her face full of warmth and devotion.

pages.caption: Her grandmother, |who lived in another village, |made her a present of a little red riding-hood
pages.scene: The interior of the home. A bright red riding-hood is draped over a chair, freshly made.

pages.caption: Which became her so well that every one called her Little Red Riding-Hood
pages.scene: The village. The girl wears the red riding-hood, turning heads wherever she goes.

pages.caption: One day her mother, having made some custards, said to her

pages.caption: Go, my dear, and see how thy grandmamma does, for I hear she has been very ill
pages.scene: The kitchen. The mother turns to face her daughter, who stands nearby listening.

pages.caption: Carry her a custard, and this little pot of butter

pages.caption: Little Red Riding-Hood set out immediately to go to her grandmother

pages.caption: Who lived in another village

pages.caption: As she was going through the wood she met with Gaffer Wolf

pages.caption: Who had a very great mind to eat her up

pages.caption: But he dared not, because of some faggot-makers hard by in the forest
pages.scene: The forest edge. In the distance, several faggot-makers chop wood among the trees.

pages.caption: He asked her whither she was going so early
pages.scene: The forest path. The wolf approaches the girl and speaks to her.

pages.caption: The poor child, who did not know that it was dangerous to stay and hear a wolf talk
pages.scene: The forest path. The girl stands before the wolf, her basket in hand, unaware of danger.

pages.caption: Said: 'I am going to see my grandmamma and carry her a custard and a little pot of butter from my mamma'
pages.scene: The forest path. The girl speaks openly to the wolf, gesturing toward her grandmother's village.

pages.caption: 'Does she live far off?' said the Wolf
pages.scene: The forest path. The wolf tilts his head curiously, asking about the distance.

pages.caption: 'It is beyond that mill you see there, at the first house in the village'
pages.scene: The forest path. Beyond the trees, a mill is visible in the distance. The girl points toward it.

pages.caption: 'Well, and I'll go and see her too. I'll go this way and you go that'
pages.scene: The forest path. The wolf grins and proposes a race, his tail swishing.

pages.caption: 'We shall see who will be there soonest'
pages.scene: The forest path. The wolf and the girl face each other, each preparing to take a different direction.

pages.caption: The Wolf began to run as fast as he could, taking the nearest way
pages.scene: The forest. The wolf bolts through the trees at full speed, his paws kicking up dirt and leaves.

pages.caption: While the little girl went by that farthest about

pages.caption: Diverting herself in gathering nuts
pages.scene: A forest clearing with tall nut-bearing trees. The girl kneels on the ground.

pages.caption: Running after butterflies
pages.scene: A sunlit forest glade. Colorful butterflies flutter among wildflowers.

pages.caption: And making nosegays of such little flowers as she met with
pages.scene: A forest path lined with small wildflowers. The girl bends to pick blossoms.

pages.caption: 'Who's there?'

pages.scene: Grandmother's bedroom. The girl climbs onto the bed and pulls the covers over herself.

pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl lies beside the figure and stares at the night-clothes.

pages.caption: Said to her: 'Grandmamma, what great arms you have got!'
pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl's eyes widen as she notices the large arms.

pages.caption: 'That is the better to hug thee, my dear'

pages.caption: 'Grandmamma, what great legs you have got!'
pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl glances down at the large legs beneath the covers.

pages.caption: 'That is to run the better, my child'

pages.caption: 'Grandmamma, what great ears you have got!'
pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl notices the enormous ears sticking up from the pillow.

pages.caption: 'That is to hear the better, my child'

pages.caption: 'Grandmamma, what great eyes you have got!'
pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl stares into the large, glaring eyes.

pages.caption: 'It is to see the better, my child'

pages.scene: Grandmother's bed. The girl notices the sharp, white teeth glistening.
